text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

BARLEY SALE - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it accepted the tender of L. Dreyfus Negoce Paris for the supply of 25,000 tonnes of barley at $145.39 per tonne. Prices include C and F Limassol, Cyprus, the commission said in a statement. Shipment is scheduled between October 15 and 30.

WHEAT SALE - South Korean feed mill companies, including Sunjin Feed Co Ltd and Jeil Feed Mill Co Ltd, on Friday bought 52,000 tonnes of feed wheat at $141.90 per tonne, C&F. Traders said Toepfer won the contract with arrival for January 10 to Inchon. Origin of the wheat was set on seller's option with shipment for November 22 to December 11, if the wheat was from Europe, or for December 12-31 if it was from Canada, Australia or the Pacific Northwest.

CORN, SOYBEAN AND WHEAT TENDER - Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold three tenders next week for a total of 72,000 tonnes of corn, 12,000 tonnes of soybeans and between 64,000 and 96,000 tonnes of wheat. Taiwanese traders expect Taiwan Sugar Corp to tender for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans. Taiwan Sugar's shipment is slated for delivery from the U.S. Gulf from Oct 25 to Nov 10. Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group is expected to tender for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn. The FGEP shipment would be for delivery from December 10-25 from U.S. Gulf or between December 26 to January 9 from PNW.

WHEAT TENDER - Armenia will be seeking 21,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for up to November 20 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. The wheat would come from the European Community, Ukraine or if U.S. origin, only hard red winter no.2. The latest date for offers was Oct 14, Yerevan, Armenia.
- Slovenia was expected to tender early next week for 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes U.S. hard red spring wheat, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for October 12-November 15.
- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to place a tender within two weeks for two 34,000-tonne shipments of U.S. wheat, local traders said. No details were available.

WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Sri Lanka is to seek October 18 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat. It seeks 50,000 tonnes soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will soon invite bids for 50,000 tonnes of rice for November/December delivery, officials of the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment (CWE) said. The new purchase will be for delivery in November and December and there will be no restrictions on rice origin.

MARKET TALK - European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler early on Friday defended EU export subsidies for wheat and vowed the EU would refrain from undercutting American wheat on the international market.

... Asian traders were anticipating a soymeal price war once Chinese buyers get over their National Day holiday, Hong Kong trading sources said ... Indications are that China bought at least 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal overnight for October shipment, U.S. exporters said. One exporter said China bought 44 percent protein meal. Another exporter was unable to confirm the quantity but said China did buy soymeal. Rumors in the U.S. soybean market at mid-week had China seeking 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal.

... Hong Kong rice traders on Friday signed a memorandum of understanding to import 270,000 tonnes of top-grade Thai fragrant rice in 1997 against 265,000 tonnes expected to be lifted this year, Thai Commerce Minister Chucheep Hansawat said. Chucheep said Hong Kong rice buyers would hold quarterly negotiations on the price of the Thai rice they plan to buy next year.
